incidents.summary: Investigative reporting alleged that Imperial Brands’ confidential Laos tobacco agreement froze taxes for 25 years and delivered millions of dollars to a relative of the country’s former leader.

sources.title: How a Secret Tobacco Deal in Laos Enriched a Political Insider – The Diplomat
sources.quote: A confidential contract between tobacco giant Imperial Brands and Laos has delivered millions of dollars to a relative of the impoverished Southeast Asian country’s former leader, documents obtained by The Examination show.

sources.title: How a Secret Tobacco Deal in Laos Enriched a Political Insider – The Diplomat
sources.quote: Signed behind closed doors in 2001, the contract includes a 25-year tax freeze that has kept cigarette prices among the lowest in the world while smoking rates in the communist nation have remained among the highest in the region.

incidents.summary: 2ONE Labs and Performance Plus Marketing sued Imperial subsidiaries over alleged Zone trademark infringement and allegedly false statements used to obtain the trademark.

sources.title: 2ONE Labs and Performance Plus Marketing, sellers of 2ONE
sources.quote: The suit alleges that Imperial’s Zone products infringe the 2ONE® tobacco-free nicotine pouch brand and that the infringement is willful.

sources.title: 2ONE Labs and Performance Plus Marketing, sellers of 2ONE
sources.quote: The suit alleges Imperial Brands made false statements by claiming a significantly earlier use of their mark in commerce than had occurred.

sources.title: 2ONE Labs and Performance Plus Marketing, sellers of 2ONE
sources.quote: The case (number 2:24-cv-08124) is before the US District Court for the Central District of California, and is styled 2ONE Labs, Inc., and Performance Plus Marketing, Inc. vs. ITG Brands, LLC and Imperial Tobacco Limited.

incidents.summary: Imperial and BAT sought to strike out a claim by Malawi farmers alleging multi-year exploitation involving child labour and forced labour.

sources.title: Tobacco firms in move to strike out Malawi exploitation case | Tobacco industry | The Guardian
sources.quote: BAT and Imperial will on Wednesday ask the high court in London to dismiss watershed proceedings

sources.title: British American Tobacco and Imperial aim to strike out claims by impoverished Malawi farmers
sources.quote: the companies’ actions, for the sake of maximising profits, have resulted over many years in their systemic exploitation.

sources.title: British American Tobacco and Imperial aim to strike out claims by impoverished Malawi farmers
sources.quote: Their conditions of work amount to child labour, forced labour, unlawful compulsory labour and exploitation under Malawian law.
